proof_boundary: The artifact proves exact exhaustion, scale, chart, and conditional composition identities. It does not prove the Xi relative old-collar estimate, Lambda<=0, RH, PF-infinity, or the Clay prize.

rows.claim: An exponential-radius exhaustion keeps every newly entering strip on the already proved explicit tL=25 ray.
rows.proof_boundary: This changes the exhaustion geometry; it does not control the old descendant collars.

rows.claim: The minimum scaled time on the new strip from R_j to R_(j+1) is exactly 25.
rows.proof_boundary: Uses x>=R_j and monotonicity of L(x).

rows.claim: The existing dominant-saddle theorem excludes every first-jet contact on every new strip of the explicit schedule.
rows.proof_boundary: Imports the checked dominant-saddle global-ray theorem. No claim is made below tL=25.

rows.claim: The ray-aligned rectangles are cofinal in positive time and finite frequency.
rows.proof_boundary: Cofinality alone does not certify the rectangles.

rows.claim: After the schedule change, the only all-stage successor antecedent is transport on the old collar.
rows.formula: C_j^out=[t_(j+1),t_j]x[38,R_j]; S_j=[t_(j+1),1/2]x[R_j,R_(j+1)] is already contact-free; x<=38 is independently closed
rows.proof_boundary: A relative old-collar estimate is still open and is the remaining infinite-dimensional Xi input.

rows.claim: The reciprocal-square blend is a smooth positive scale joining the parabolic and frequency coordinates.
rows.proof_boundary: Positive scaling preserves contacts and degree but does not itself prove a relative Xi estimate.

rows.claim: The two chart weights form an exact unit partition and the blended scale stays within sqrt(2) of the smaller natural scale.
rows.proof_boundary: The comparison is conditioning control, not a lower bound for the Xi first jet.

rows.claim: The scale-variation terms are explicit and locally integrable at every positive time.
rows.proof_boundary: The time derivative is singular at t=0, as required by the arbitrary-multiplicity Hermite model.

rows.claim: A relative bound in either natural chart transfers to the blended chart with at most sqrt(2) conditioning loss in that chart's regime.
rows.proof_boundary: The inequalities are conditional on Xi relative bounds kappa_par or kappa_freq; neither bound is asserted here.

rows.claim: Every new point enters deeply in the frequency chart, then moves continuously toward the parabolic chart as its fixed spatial coordinate descends toward t=0.
rows.formula: on entry q=2t_(j+1)L_j^2=50L_j>=5050; for fixed x, q=2tL(x)^2->0 as t->0
rows.proof_boundary: Chart conditioning is exact; descendant noncontact still requires the relative Xi inequality.

rows.claim: The ray-aligned old-collar logarithmic time ratio tends to zero, so a K/t descendant estimate has vanishing one-step cost.
rows.proof_boundary: An infinite product may tend to zero; the induction needs only a positive factor at each finite stage.

rows.claim: The same schedule can be placed on any fixed c=c_*+epsilon ray above its existential threshold.
rows.proof_boundary: The oscillatory-zeta theorem supplies an existential L_epsilon; the explicit c=25 schedule avoids hiding it.

rows.claim: The published upper-time input, explicit new-strip ray, and relative blended-jet transport on every old collar would certify a cofinal family and imply Lambda<=0. Equivalently, one relative theorem on the inner wedge 0<t<=min(1/4,25/L(x)) is sufficient.
rows.formula: if ||partial_t(H,s_pf H_x)||<=kappa_j(t)||(H,s_pf H_x)|| on C_j^out with integral_(t_(j+1))^(t_j)kappa_j<infinity for every j, then every P_j is contact-free; equivalently tau(x)=min(1/4,25/L(x)) and an integrable relative bound on 0<t<=tau(x), x>=38, suffices
rows.proof_boundary: The relative old-collar antecedent is unproved. Therefore this row is not RH or a Clay-prize proof.

rows.claim: Construct an a priori two-chart relative majorant for the exact Xi heat flow on the ray-aligned descendant collars, with a finite bounded-L transition and without dividing by the unknown first-jet norm.
rows.formula: q<=1: establish kappa_par=O(1/t) in the Hermite chart; q>=1 below the entry ray: establish an integrable frequency-chart bound; kappa must not be defined as ||partial_t V_pf||/||V_pf||
rows.proof_boundary: On each compact positive-time interval, mere existence of an integrable relative bound is equivalent to nonvanishing: the reverse implication takes kappa=||partial_t V_pf||/||V_pf||. The required a priori majorant is the remaining RH-level analytic obligation.

status: exact ray-aligned exhaustion and parabolic-frequency scale reduction with one open Xi descendant antecedent
